speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing both psychiatric symptoms and a new movement disorder; to help me understand your condition, can you tell me what specific movements you are noticing, such as tremors, rigidity, or involuntary jerking?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful information; the timing of these movements shortly after starting risperidone is significant. Are these movements present in your hands or feet, and do they stop or disappear when you are sleeping?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms describe akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Does this restlessness cause you significant anxiety or difficulty sitting through your classes? I also need to check your vital signs to rule out other causes.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of risperidone use and symptoms of restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to stay still, this is highly suggestive of drug-induced akathisia. To confirm this, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started in relation to beginning the medication? DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Akathisia
